glossary.Transient: Lasting only a short time and then going away.
glossary.Reflex: An automatic, involuntary nervous system response to a stimulus.
glossary.Simple faint: Everyday term for vasovagal syncope: brief collapse with quick, full recovery.
glossary.Loss of consciousness: A state of being unaware and unresponsive to surroundings.
glossary.Cerebral hypoperfusion: Not enough blood flow reaching the brain.
glossary.Lightheadedness: A feeling of being about to faint, woozy or unsteady.
glossary.Tinnitus: Ringing or buzzing heard in the ears without an outside sound.
glossary.Diaphoresis: Heavy sweating, often a sign of autonomic activation.
glossary.Nausea: Feeling sick, as if about to vomit.
glossary.Seizure: A burst of abnormal electrical activity in the brain causing altered behaviour or convulsions.
glossary.Epileptic activity: Abnormal, synchronised firing of brain neurones that causes a seizure.
glossary.Arrhythmia: An abnormal heart rhythm, too fast, too slow or irregular.
glossary.Cardiac syncope: Fainting caused by a heart problem such as an arrhythmia; more dangerous than vasovagal.
glossary.Autonomic nervous system: Part of the nervous system controlling automatic functions like heart rate and blood vessel tone.
glossary.Vagus nerve: Tenth cranial nerve; carries parasympathetic signals that slow the heart.
glossary.Vagal reflex: Reflex through the vagus nerve that slows the heart and lowers blood pressure.
glossary.Systemic vascular resistance: Resistance to blood flow across all the body's arteries; falls when vessels dilate.
glossary.Blood pressure: Pressure of blood in the arteries; set by cardiac output times vascular resistance.
glossary.Basic bloods: Routine tests such as full blood count, urea and electrolytes and glucose.
glossary.Work-up: The set of tests used to investigate a symptom.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination, without needing a confirmatory test.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available test or method for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.Hydration: Having enough fluid in the body; helps maintain blood volume.
glossary.Elevate the legs: Raising the legs above the heart to push blood back to the central circulation.
glossary.Myoclonic: Describing sudden, brief, involuntary muscle jerks.
glossary.Uncomplicated: Without any added problems or high-risk features.
glossary.NICE: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence; publishes clinical guidelines in England.
glossary.CG109: NICE guideline on transient loss of consciousness ('blackouts') in people over 16.
glossary.Blackout: Lay term for a transient loss of consciousness.
